Shown a correct program of another algorithm and told not to use it, the model goes home to its default. How often a ban is obeyed depends on its wording more than on anything else measured, and the template that states only that the algorithm is not allowed here is the weakest in every artifact and model tested. A ban of five names is obeyed by name far more often than by mechanism. Read by runtime expansion order over 546 programs in ten configurations, lexical compliance exceeds mechanistic compliance by 0.70 (runtime label) or 0.61 (tracer), in every configuration, and in the three configurations with reasoning nearly every covert program comes with reasoning that names a banned algorithm; the tracer failed its gold gate on iterative deepening, so these numbers are descriptive. The gap is a property of exhausting the repertoire. Under cumulative bans of one to five names, Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-14B with thinking comply by name and by mechanism at one name (1.00), and mechanistic compliance falls to 0.22 and 0.10 at five names while lexical compliance stays at or above 0.86.
